title: Regulations — Race rules 2025 (Lavaredo Ultra Trail by UTMB)
publisher: La Sportiva Lavaredo Ultra Trail by UTMB
claims: The regulations page is headed 'Race rules 2025' and carries no 2026 or 2027 label, while it sits in the navigation of the 2027 event site.

Semi-autonomy means runners must carry all mandatory equipment throughout the race, in a pack, may not remove it on course, and may be checked at any time; refusing an equipment check is a disqualification.
Refreshment stations provide drinks and food for consumption on site, and the organisation only supplies still water and/or sports drink for refilling bottles and packs.

For the 100M and 100K races a personal assistant is allowed at certain aid stations in a reserved area; for the 50K race only at certain events; one assistant only, with a bag of at most 30 litres, medical assistance by the assistant is forbidden, and the assistance zone starts 500 m before and ends 500 m after the aid station.
It is forbidden to accompany or be accompanied by a non-registered person outside the clearly defined tolerance zones around aid stations.
Runners may not take part with a dog or any other animal, including service animals.

Equipment checks may be organised at any point or carried out randomly during the race; missing a listed safety item leads to disqualification, missing other mandatory items to a one-hour penalty, and refusing a check to disqualification.

Trekking poles, if used, must be carried for the whole race; starting without poles and collecting them later is forbidden, poles may not be placed in spare bags, and they may be banned in marked areas.
Earphones are tolerated if used safely; they must be removed when crossing roads and at checkpoints.

Each runner receives a spare bag of at least 30 litres at race-pack collection; only UTMB World Series bags are accepted; bags are returned on presentation of the bib and must be collected within two hours of the end of the race; only organisation bags are transported and poles are not allowed inside them.
Littering is forbidden; bins are available at each aid station and runners must carry their waste to the next one; plastic bags for soiled paper are handed out with the bibs.

Medical stations are linked to a command centre with medical staff at the centre or on the course; medical staff can remove a participant, demand mandatory equipment, evacuate and refer runners, and a runner treated with an intravenous drip must withdraw; there is a medical centre at the finish.

Cut-off times are leave-by times: runners must leave the checkpoint or aid station before the cut-off whatever their arrival time; when the start is in several waves, the maximum time and the barriers are calculated from the last wave.
Runners who drop out, are stopped or arrive behind a time barrier may not continue, have their bib cut and are transported by the organisation.

Dropouts must be reported at a checkpoint; runners who withdraw keep their bib for transport, meals and treatment rooms; vehicles are available at some aid stations and runners elsewhere must make their own way to the nearest repatriation point.
Some aid stations have rest areas with camp beds and blankets.

At UTMB World Series Events the first five men and first five women overall, plus the first man and woman in each age category, receive a trophy; awards are handed out only at the prize-giving ceremony and attendance is mandatory.
Age categories run 16-17, 18-19, 20-34, then five-year bands up to 85+.

The 100K/100M penalty chart gives disqualification for missing a key safety item (no minimum water, no waterproof jacket with hood, no torch, no survival blanket, no smartphone), a one-hour penalty for other missing mandatory items, 15 minutes for a phone switched off or in airplane mode, one hour for littering, disqualification for refusing an equipment check or not assisting a person in need, one hour for assistance outside authorised zones, 15 minutes for being accompanied outside tolerance zones, lifetime disqualification for cheating, 15 minutes for a non-visible bib, one hour for using poles not carried from the start and two hours for starting in an earlier wave than assigned.
